svg.title: Self-Managed Truck Parking Yard Operating Model
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-truck-parking-yard-operating-model; chapter number: 11; title: Self-Managed Truck Parking Yard Operating Model; subtitle: One operator, automated gates and a marketplace channel; caption: Operators self-manage yards with Easy Storage, PDK text-to-gate or Rig Hut app access tied to payment, and Truck Parking Club hosts start on a 70/30 split.; assumptions note: Practitioners did not report staff counts; the hub reflects the self-managed setups they describe. Spoke KPIs are the figures stated by Ronald Rohde, Truck Parking Media and REtipster's Evan Shelley interview.; note: Sources: Truck Parking Media (ulBXkeE5I_8 @ 00:02:30, 00:02:13); Ronald Rohde Law (rPXHwXgqWs8 @ 00:06:59, tonuCLfZrYE @ 00:14:14); REtipster (Ombo8TjihMk @ 00:12:41).; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Yard Owner-Operator; headcount: Self-managed through yard software and gate automation; focus: By-right zoning, stall rent, and average revenue per space net of bad debt, vacancy and late payments; spokes: role: Inbound Booking Line; type: In-house, answer-first; kpi: Caller entered into the system immediately; a 20-minute callback lost bookings; role: Gate and Access Control; type: Automation (PDK text-to-gate or Rig Hut app); kpi: Access tied to payment; 30 ft cantilever about $30K installed; role: Truck Parking Club Listing; type: Marketplace platform; kpi: 70/30 owner/platform starting split, lower for 5-10 lot operators; role: Class A Service Vendors; type: Outsourced with markup; kpi: Wash billed at $225 against a $200 vendor price; patrol about $5K/mo
